title: Who says no
question: How often does each supervisor vote no on a money file, and how often alone?
finding: Supervisors cast 37,421 aye or no votes at the final vote on money files from 2015 to 9 November 2026; 215 (0.6%) were no votes. Among the 33 members with 100 or more such votes the share runs from 0.0% to 3.2% (Dean Preston, 50 of 1,540). The most no votes: Dean Preston 50 (43 as the only no, on 19 meeting days); Aaron Peskin 30 (13 as the only no, on 27 meeting days); Catherine Stefani 18 (12 as the only no, on 11 meeting days); Jane Kim 14 (0 as the only no, on 13 meeting days). 6 of the 33 never voted no on a money file: Alan Wong, Bilal Mahmood, Chyanne Chen, Danny Sauter, Stephen Sherrill, Vallie Brown. At the committee stage 20 of 10,184 votes on a recommendation were noes.
how: One row per member as the vote pages print the name. “Final votes cast” counts ayes and noes at the final Board roll call on money files; lines printed as excused or absent are not votes and are left out. “The only no” counts roll calls where the member was the single dissenter, and “meeting days” the separate dates of the member’s noes, because one no repeated down a day’s list of files is counted once per file. Committee columns count ayes and noes on roll calls that recommend a money file or send it on. First and last roll call are the member’s first and last line anywhere in these tables.
limits: Voting no is a member’s job as much as voting aye, and the count says nothing about the files or the member’s motives. Members served for different years and sat on different committees, so counts are not like for like: a member of the budget committees casts far more committee votes. A member who votes against the annual budget and the files that travel with it collects many noes in one afternoon. “Excused” is printed for a member who was out of the room or away as well as for one excused from voting; the page does not say which, and it is never read here as anything else. The Rules of Order say: “Every Supervisor present when a question is put shall vote for or against it, unless excused from voting by motion.” For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
